blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Port Moody total for houses that month.

blocks.text: College Park Houses: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is detached houses on the Clarke Road and College Park Way side of the city's west end, under the RS zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 2937.
The College Park Elementary building stands at 300 Princeton Avenue, but the building does not appear in School District No. 43's current Port Moody school list.

blocks.text: College Park Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Johns Street route, so its west edge is a municipal boundary, not just a street.

The City plans College Park together with Harbour Heights, Glenayre and Seaview in one Chapter 14 section, so Official Community Plan reading for this pocket is a four-neighbourhood section, not a College Park chapter.
Seaview's stated extent — College Park Way to Ingersoll Street, Seaforth Way to Glenayre Drive — is the closest thing to a boundary the City publishes for this cluster.
Barnet Highway (Highway 7A) and St. Johns Street run east–west through the city, and Clarke Road serves the College Park and Glenayre side streets.
Glenayre Drive ties the pocket to Glenayre and the Glenayre Centre at 492 Glencoe Drive.

blocks.text: The road that opened up this side of Port Moody

The Barnet Highway, the main road west from this side of Port Moody to North Burnaby and Vancouver, began as a five-mile wagon road to a lumber mill at the foot of Burnaby Mountain, finished in 1903. It was fully paved around 1930 and widened to four lanes with HOV lanes in the 1990s, a $105 million project, so College Park’s houses, typically built in the 1970s, have always had a direct route into the city.
